what_its_for: This antibiotic is used to treat bacterial infections such as ear infections, sinus infections, pneumonia, skin infections, and urinary tract infections. It works by killing the bacteria causing your infection. It will NOT work for colds, flu, or other viral infections.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with food or milk to help prevent an upset stomach and diarrhea. Swallow tablets or capsules whole — do not crush or chew them. If you are using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each use and measure your dose carefully with the measuring device that came with your medicine — never use a regular kitchen spoon. Take every dose at evenly spaced times throughout the day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body. Finish ALL of the medicine even if you feel better before it is gone.
dosing: Your dose depends on your age, weight, the type of infection being treated, and your kidney function. Your doctor or pharmacist will tell you exactly how much to take and how often. Adults are commonly prescribed 500 mg every 8 hours or 875 mg every 12 hours. Children are usually dosed based on their body weight. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not change your dose without asking your doctor or pharmacist first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tablets and capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C), away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Keep the medicine out of the bathroom. The mixed liquid (suspension) must be kept in the refrigerator — do NOT freeze it. Throw away any unused liquid after 10 days. Keep all medicine out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium at the same time as this medicine, as they can reduce how well it works — space them at least 2 hours apart. Do not take extra doses or share this medicine with others. Avoid alcohol as it may increase the risk of side effects like stomach upset. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines you take, especially blood thinners like warfarin, other antibiotics, or the gout medicine probenecid, as they can interact with this medication.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction (hives, rash, swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, difficulty breathing or swallowing); severe or bloody diarrhea or stomach cramps, which may be a sign of a serious bowel infection; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) or dark urine, which could indicate liver problems; severe skin reactions such as blistering or peeling; or if your infection does not seem to be getting better after a few days of treatment. Also call your doctor if you develop a new vaginal yeast infection, as this can happen when taking antibiotics.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting this medicine. However, it is very important to keep taking ALL of your doses until the prescription is finished, even if your symptoms go away sooner. Stopping early can allow the bacteria to come back stronger and harder to treat.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor may lower your dose if your kidneys do not work well. Tell your doctor if you are on dialysis. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is generally considered safe during pregnancy, but always tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking it. Children: Dosing is based on your child's weight — always follow your doctor's exact instructions. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to this medicine, especially regarding stomach side effects. Allergies: Do NOT take this medicine if you have ever had a severe allergic reaction to penicillin, amoxicillin, or any other beta-lactam antibiotic. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all your allergies.
